title: The Parrot with the Broken Wing (MR)
summary: Akbar rescues an injured parrot in the royal gardens and nurses it back to health. Birbal shows the court that kindness is the true measure of kingship.
full_text:
During a morning walk in the gardens of Fatehpur Sikri, Emperor Akbar heard a faint, piteous fluttering in the rose bushes. Looking down, he discovered a young green parrot with a broken wing, bleeding and unable to fly, with a hungry stray cat creeping toward it.

Without hesitation, Emperor Akbar stepped forward, chased the cat away, gently lifted the trembling bird in his silk handkerchief, and carried it to his private pavilion.

For three weeks, the Emperor of Hindustan—ruler of fifty million subjects—personally cleaned the bird's wound, applied herbal poultices, and fed it sweet mango pulp and seeds with his own hands. When the wing finally healed and the parrot fluttered to the marble railing, Akbar opened his hands and watched the bird soar joyfully into the blue sky.

A cynical courtier murmured: 'Sire, was it fitting for the Great Mughal to spend hours bandaging a worthless wild bird that cannot even speak or pay tribute?'

Birbal, who had observed the Emperor's care with deep respect, turned to the courtier:

'My lord, you measure the world by tribute and profit. But true greatness is measured by compassion toward those who can offer nothing in return.

'An emperor can command armies, execute enemies, and build golden palaces through power alone. But when an emperor bends his royal knee to cradle an injured wild bird, preserve its fragile life, and set it free to fly in the heavens, he mirrors the mercy of the Almighty Creator!

'Power makes a monarch feared, but mercy makes a monarch beloved in heaven and earth.'

Akbar smiled warmly and clasped Birbal's hand, affirming that a ruler's heart must remain tender to the humblest creature under his sky.
